Title: Transmission of Persistent Temporary Public-Spending Shocks: Advanced Economies
Subtitle: (Deviations from steady state; units vary by panel)
Notes: Note: Impulse responses to four standard debt-financed expansion shocks, each a persistent (AR(1), persistence 0.9) increase in one spending category with an impact of 1 percent of GDP and no offsetting cut, as listed in the legend. All panels report deviations from the steady state, calculated by block. Panels in the top three rows are percent deviations from the steady-state level; the third row reports labor supply, human capital, effective labor, and education time. The real marginal-cost panel (the first panel of the fourth row) uses the same units. Inflation and the nominal and real interest rates are annualized percentage-point deviations, calculated as the change in the gross quarterly rate multiplied by 400. Fiscal panels (bottom row: primary deficit, transfers, debt-to-GDP ratio) are deviations in percentage points of steady-state GDP. The real interest rate is the nominal interest rate deflated by inflation.

Title: Reallocation of Expenditure: Advanced Economies
Subtitle: (Percent deviation from steady state)
Notes: Note: Output responses (percent deviation from steady state) to a permanent increase of 1 percent of GDP in the expenditure categories listed in the legend, funded by a cut in public consumption.

Title: Reallocation of Expenditure: Emerging Market and Developing Economies
Subtitle: (Percent deviation from steady state)
Notes: Note: Output responses (percent deviation from steady state) to a permanent increase of 1 percent of GDP in the expenditure categories listed in the legend, funded by a cut in public consumption. No R&D channel: the innovation channel is shut down for EMDEs.

Title: Transmission of Matched Permanent Spending and Efficiency Improvements
Subtitle: (Deviations from steady state; units vary by panel)
Notes: Note: Solid lines report the benchmark impulse responses to permanent 0.25-percent-of-GDP spending increases in the AE calibration, financed through debt with no offsetting cut. Dotted lines report AE efficiency improvements calibrated to generate the same increase in effective productive spending, with spending levels unchanged. Dashed lines report the corresponding matched EMDE efficiency improvements for infrastructure and human capital. The EMDE R&D response is omitted because technology creation is inactive in that calibration. Circles mark first-quarter effects, and the log-transformed quarterly axis expands the early response horizon. Columns distinguish the three spending instruments, while rows report output, consumption, the primary deficit, and public debt. Output and consumption are percent deviations from steady-state levels. The primary deficit and public debt are deviations in percentage points of steady-state GDP. The three panels within each row share a common vertical scale.

Title: Transmission of Permanent Spending-Efficiency Improvements: Emerging Market and Developing Economies
Subtitle: (Deviations from steady state; units vary by panel)
Notes: Note: Impulse responses to fully and permanently closing each calibrated spending-efficiency gap from the first quarter, with spending levels unchanged, as listed in the legend. Circles mark first-quarter effects, and the log-transformed quarterly axis expands the early response horizon. All panels report deviations from the steady state. Panels in the top three rows and the real marginal-cost panel are percent deviations from steady-state levels. Inflation and the nominal and real interest rates are annualized percentage-point deviations. Fiscal panels are deviations in percentage points of steady-state GDP. The real interest rate is the nominal interest rate deflated by inflation. The R&D channel is inactive in the EMDE calibration.

Title: Advanced Economies: Increase in Spending Efficiency
Subtitle: (Additional output gain after 25 years)
Notes: Note: Additional output gains relative to the corresponding expenditure reallocation when each calibrated AE efficiency gap is gradually closed over 25 years.

Title: Emerging Market and Developing Economies: Increase in Spending Efficiency
Subtitle: (Additional output gain after 25 years)
Notes: Note: Additional output gains relative to the corresponding expenditure reallocation when the calibrated EMDE efficiency gaps are gradually closed over 15 or 25 years. Circles show the corresponding gains from higher initial gaps. The R&D channel is inactive in the EMDE calibration.

Title: Advanced Economies: Combining Human Capital and R&D
Subtitle: (Percent deviation from steady state)
Notes: Note: Output gains (percent deviation from steady state) from increasing public investment in human capital, public spending on research and development (R&D), and a 50/50 mix of both, financed by cutting public consumption.

Title: Advanced Economies: High versus Low Levels of Technology Diffusion, 2050
Subtitle: (Percent deviation from steady state)
Notes: Note: Output gains (percent deviation from steady state) from a 50/50 human-capital/R&D spending mix for different levels of technology diffusion.

Title: Estimated Spending-Efficiency Gaps by Income Group, 2000–23
Subtitle: (Efficiency gap, one minus the spending efficiency score)
Notes: Note: Appendix figure. Efficiency gap (one minus the spending efficiency score) for infrastructure, health, education, and R&D. Shaded areas show the 25th–75th percentile range across economies within each income group; lines are group medians; circles mark the 2023 value, the calibration reference. R&D is shown for advanced economies only, as the innovation channel is shut down for EMDEs. The paper's human capital gap e^GE combines the health and education categories.

Title: Data Underlying Country-Group Calibration Targets, 2000–23
Subtitle: (Units vary by panel)
Sources: Source: IMF World Economic Outlook database; Bachas and others 2024; IMF staff calculations.
Notes: Note: Appendix figure. Solid lines are equal-country group medians, dotted lines are calendar-GDP-weighted group averages, and shaded areas show the 25th–75th percentile range across countries. Circles mark 2023 medians except for the labor-income tax, whose latest observation is 2018. Open diamonds show the corresponding Table 2 calibration targets. For the consumption-tax panel, the weighted line aggregates the tax and consumption-base components before calculating the implicit rate. Real GDP growth is the annual percentage change in constant-price GDP. Government investment is general-government fixed investment; its model counterpart sums infrastructure and human-capital investment and excludes public R&D. The labor-income tax is the effective tax rate on labor income from Bachas and others (2024), excluding indirect taxes. Public debt is general-government gross debt as a percentage of GDP.

Title: Persistent Temporary Government-Consumption Shock under Progressive Model Simplification: Advanced Economies
Subtitle: (Deviations from steady state; units vary by panel)
Notes: Note: Impulse responses to a persistent AR(1) government-consumption increase with persistence 0.9, an impact of 1 percent of GDP, and no offsetting cut. The seven cumulative steps remove endogenous technology, human capital, public infrastructure, private capital, price indexation, trend growth, and the extended fiscal block. The solid red endpoint is derived from the full model; the dashed black line is an independently coded canonical control, and their responses coincide. Circles mark first-quarter impact responses, and the log-transformed quarterly axis expands the early response horizon. Inactive channels appear as flat or missing lines. Demand, supply, labor, and real marginal cost are percent deviations from steady-state levels. Inflation and interest rates are annualized percentage-point deviations. Fiscal panels are deviations in percentage points of steady-state GDP.

Title: Sensitivity of Output Responses to Structural Parameters under Persistent Temporary Shocks: Advanced Economies
Subtitle: (Percent deviation from steady state)
Notes: Note: Output responses (percent deviation from steady state) to a debt-financed expansion of 1 percent of GDP (persistent AR(1), persistence 0.9, no offsetting cut) as one structural parameter is varied over a plausible range, one spending category and parameter per panel: the output elasticity of infrastructure (alpha_G), the elasticity of human capital formation with respect to the public human capital stock (mu), and the elasticity of technology creation with respect to public R&D (alpha_RD). In each panel the lines run from the low (light) to the high (dark) value of the parameter, with each line labeled by its parameter value at the right. The AE baseline and the EMDE value of the varied elasticity, where applicable, are highlighted only by thicker lines; their colors remain on the same panel scale, and all other parameters remain at their AE settings. No EMDE value is shown for alpha_RD because technology creation is inactive in that calibration. Circles mark first-quarter impact responses. The horizontal axis reports quarterly responses on a linear scale through the 25-year horizon, with annual labels at selected quarters; the three panels share a common vertical scale.
